Description: Name of the laboratory or institution hosting the instrument. Standard cross-TAPP identity field, distinct from the paper-sourced 'Laboratory name' field above.
Example/Allowed Content: e.g., 'NERC Isotope Geosciences Laboratory, British Geological Survey'
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — Group 1 template (mandatory in all TAPPs). Merged 2026-07-27: also covers Table 3's 'Laboratory name' item (paper example: 'Dept of Earth Science, University of Everywhere').

Description: A short descriptive name for this analytical procedure, with version number. Should include instrument/mass-analyzer configuration, technique, and target mineral or isotopic system.
Example/Allowed Content: e.g., 'LA-ICP-MS U-Pb Zircon Geochronology v1' | 'LA-SF-ICP-MS U-Th-Pb Monazite Geochronology v1'
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — Group 1 template (mandatory in all TAPPs)

Description: Top-level analytical technique identifier, including the ICP-MS mass-analyzer configuration used for in situ U-(Th-)Pb dating.
Example/Allowed Content: LA-ICP-MS U-(Th-)Pb Geochronology | LA-Q-ICP-MS U-(Th-)Pb Geochronology | LA-SF-ICP-MS U-(Th-)Pb Geochronology | LA-MC-ICP-MS U-(Th-)Pb Geochronology | Other: specify
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — Group 1 template (mandatory in all TAPPs)

Description: Person(s) or laboratory responsible for developing and registering this procedure. ORCID recommended for individuals.
Example/Allowed Content: e.g., 'M. Horstwood (ORCID: 0000-0002-9720-716X), NERC Isotope Geosciences Laboratory'
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — Group 1 template (mandatory in all TAPPs)

Description: Name(s) of the analyst(s) who performed the analysis session. ORCID recommended for persistent identification.
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — Group 1 template (mandatory in all TAPPs)

Description: Persistent identifier for the laboratory, e.g., ROR ID.
Example/Allowed Content: ROR ID or equivalent URI (https://ror.org/)
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — Group 1 template (mandatory in all TAPPs)

Description: First date this procedure configuration was used in production.
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — Group 1 template (mandatory in all TAPPs)

Description: Date on which the analytical session began. For sessions spanning multiple days, use the date of the first session.
Example/Allowed Content: YYYY-MM-DD
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — Group 1 template (mandatory in all TAPPs)

Description: Date on which the analytical session ended. May equal Analysis Start Date for single-day sessions.
Example/Allowed Content: YYYY-MM-DD
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — Group 1 template (mandatory in all TAPPs)

Description: DOI or unique persistent identifier for the registered procedure used in this analysis. Mandatory when submitting analytical data, to encourage formal procedure registration. Enter 'pending' if applied for but not yet minted.
Example/Allowed Content: e.g., http://doi.org/10.60520/IEDA/114187 | pending
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — Group 1 template (mandatory in all TAPPs)

Description: Grants and other funding sources that supported instrument purchase, major upgrades, and procedure development. Include grant numbers and funding agencies.
Example/Allowed Content: e.g., 'NERC IP-1332-0512' | 'None'
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — Group 1 template (mandatory in all TAPPs)

Description: Grants and other funding sources that supported the specific sample analyses reported here. Distinct from procedure development funding.
Example/Allowed Content: e.g., 'NSF EAR-1524297' | 'None'
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — Group 1 template (mandatory in all TAPPs)

Description: DOI or URL for peer-reviewed publications or technical reports describing, validating, or benchmarking this procedure.
Example/Allowed Content: e.g., doi:10.1111/j.1751-908X.2016.00379.x (Horstwood et al. 2016, community reporting standard)
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — Group 1 template (mandatory in all TAPPs)

Description: Other analytical techniques applied to the same sample(s) whose results are intended to be interpreted together with, or used to independently validate, this dataset. Enter 'None' if no coupling is intended.
Example/Allowed Content: CA-ID-TIMS | SIMS | EPMA | CL/BSE Imaging | Other: specify | None
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — Group 1 template — standard coupling field (mandatory in all TAPPs)

Description: Describes (1) the functional relationship between this dataset and the coupled technique, and (2) the analytical sequence — which technique was performed first and why. Required when Coupled Technique(s) is not 'None'.
Example/Allowed Content: e.g., 'A subset of dated grains were subsequently analysed by CA-ID-TIMS to independently validate the LA-ICP-MS age population; CA-ID-TIMS performed after LA-ICP-MS screening identified target grains'
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — Group 1 template — standard coupling field (mandatory in all TAPPs)

Description: Registered procedure DOI for the coupled technique named above.
Example/Allowed Content: e.g., pending | None
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — Group 1 template — standard coupling field (mandatory in all TAPPs)

Description: DOI or persistent identifier for the co-registered dataset or publication reporting both datasets together.
Example/Allowed Content: e.g., 'same submission' | pending | None
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — Group 1 template — standard coupling field (mandatory in all TAPPs)

Description: Pre-ablation characterisation imaging (typically cathodoluminescence [CL] or backscattered electron [BSE]) used to reveal internal zoning, inherited cores, and metamict domains for selecting valid spot locations, including the imaging instrument and settings used.
Example/Allowed Content: CL, FEI Quanta600, 10 nA, 17 mm working distance
Comments: Source: Table 3 (Horstwood et al. 2016)

Description: General description of the U-(Th-)Pb-bearing mineral(s) this procedure is designed to analyse. Used for discoverability and procedure matching.
Example/Allowed Content: Zircon | Monazite | Titanite | Apatite | Rutile | Xenotime | Baddeleyite | Perovskite | Allanite | Other: specify
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — Rule 1 shared Group 2 field (standard name mandatory in all TAPPs). Merged 2026-07-27: also covers Table 3's 'Sample type/mineral' item (paper example: 'Detrital zircons').

Description: Standard cross-TAPP description of how samples were prepared for analysis (mounting, polishing, coating, etc.).
Example/Allowed Content: Conventional mineral separation, 1 inch resin mount, 1 µm polish to finish
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — Rule 1 shared Group 2 field (standard name mandatory in all TAPPs). Merged 2026-07-27: replaces Table 3's separate 'Sample preparation' item; example is Table 3's own value. Tier corrected 2026-07-28 to Basic/Editable to match LA-Q/SF-ICP-MS TAPP v4.

Description: Name or identifier of the sample analysed, as used in the laboratory. Should match the identifier used in associated publications or data tables.
Example/Allowed Content: e.g., 'NWA 7533 zrn-14' | 'Jack Hills detrital zircon JH-22'
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — Group 2 universal field (mandatory in all TAPPs)

Description: Globally unique, persistent identifier for the analysed sample. IGSN is the recommended standard for geological and cosmochemical samples.
Example/Allowed Content: e.g., IGSN: IEDA-100001 (https://www.igsn.org/)
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — Group 2 universal field (mandatory in all TAPPs)

Description: Procedure applied immediately before each analysis to remove surface contamination or condition the sample surface, distinct from general sample preparation. Pre-ablation pulses are typically discarded before signal acquisition begins.
Example/Allowed Content: e.g., '10 pre-ablation pulses discarded before acquisition (25 µm, 5 Hz, 2.5 J cm⁻²)' | 'None'
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — imported from LA-Q/SF-ICP-MS TAPP v4

Description: Manufacturer and model of the laser ablation system.
Example/Allowed Content: ESI/New Wave Research, UP193FX
Comments: Source: Table 3 (Horstwood et al. 2016) — restructured/split for cross-TAPP consistency with LA-Q/SF-ICP-MS TAPP; field renamed from 'Make, Model and Type (Laser Ablation System)'; wavelength/type content moved to 'Laser Wavelength and Type' below.

Description: Wavelength and type of the laser used for ablation, in nanometres. Table 3 (Horstwood et al. 2016) states wavelength only; laser type (e.g., ArF excimer) is not explicitly stated for this instrument in the source example.
Example/Allowed Content: 193 nm
Comments: Source: Table 3 (Horstwood et al. 2016) — restructured/split for cross-TAPP consistency with LA-Q/SF-ICP-MS TAPP; field renamed from Group 4's 'Laser Wavelength (nm)' and relocated to Group 3, matching LA-Q/SF-ICP-MS TAPP's placement of wavelength as a fixed hardware fact.

Description: Manufacturer and model of the ICP-MS instrument.
Example/Allowed Content: Nu Instruments, Nu Plasma HR
Comments: Source: Table 3 (Horstwood et al. 2016) — restructured/split for cross-TAPP consistency with LA-Q/SF-ICP-MS TAPP; field renamed/split from 'Make, Model and Type (ICP-MS Instrument)'; mass-analyzer type moved to 'ICP-MS Type' below.

Description: Type of ICP-MS mass analyser and collector configuration.
Example/Allowed Content: Single-collector quadrupole (Q-ICP-MS) | Single-collector sector-field (SF-ICP-MS) | Multi-collector sector-field (MC-ICP-MS) | Other: specify
Comments: Source: Table 3 (Horstwood et al. 2016) — restructured/split for cross-TAPP consistency with LA-Q/SF-ICP-MS TAPP; split out of 'Make, Model and Type (ICP-MS Instrument)' as its own controlled-list field, matching LA-Q/SF-ICP-MS TAPP's split; example instrument in Table 3 (Nu Plasma HR) is MC-ICP-MS.

Description: Type, design origin, and internal volume of the ablation cell. Cell volume is a primary determinant of aerosol washout time and therefore the achievable time resolution of the data.
Example/Allowed Content: In-house built low volume cell, volume ca. 4 cm³
Comments: Source: Table 3 (Horstwood et al. 2016) — restructured/split for cross-TAPP consistency with LA-Q/SF-ICP-MS TAPP; field renamed from 'Ablation Cell and Volume' for cross-TAPP consistency; content (including volume, which LA-Q/SF-ICP-MS TAPP's field does not explicitly request) unchanged.

Description: Configuration by which the ablated aerosol is delivered to the plasma, including any co-aspirated tracer or spike solution (e.g., a Tl solution used for instrumental mass bias correction, or a ²³⁵U spike used for isotope dilution).
Example/Allowed Content: Ablation aerosol combined with co-aspiration of desolvated Tl-235U tracer
Comments: Source: Table 3 (Horstwood et al. 2016)

Description: Type(s) of detector(s) installed in the mass spectrometer used to measure the U-(Th-)Pb isotope beams.
Example/Allowed Content: mixed Faraday-multiple ion counting array
Comments: Source: Table 3 (Horstwood et al. 2016) — restructured/split for cross-TAPP consistency with LA-Q/SF-ICP-MS TAPP; field renamed from 'Detection System' for cross-TAPP consistency with LA-Q/SF-ICP-MS TAPP.

Metadata Item: Instrument Serial Number or Lab Identifier
Description: Serial number or laboratory-internal identifier for the specific instrument unit. Supports traceability to instrument service records.
Example/Allowed Content: e.g., 'Nu Plasma HR S/N 1234' | 'Lab unit: NIGL-MC1'
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — imported from LA-Q/SF-ICP-MS TAPP v4

Description: Geometry and designation of the sampler and skimmer cones installed during analysis.
Example/Allowed Content: Ni sample cone + standard Ni skimmer | Ni sample cone + Ni H-skimmer | N/A | None | Other: specify
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — imported from LA-Q/SF-ICP-MS TAPP v4

Description: Material composition of the sampler and skimmer cones. Nickel (Ni) is standard for most matrices; platinum (Pt) is used for high-TDS or organic-matrix samples.
Example/Allowed Content: Ni sampler and Ni skimmer | Pt sampler and Pt skimmer | N/A | None | Other: specify
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — imported from LA-Q/SF-ICP-MS TAPP v4

Description: Distance between the load coil and the sampling cone tip (mm), also called injector depth or torch position. Affects ion transmission efficiency, oxide formation, and doubly-charged species production.
Example/Allowed Content: 5 mm | Standard position (manufacturer default) | N/A | None
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — imported from LA-Q/SF-ICP-MS TAPP v4

Description: Type of plasma torch used (e.g., standard quartz, high-matrix, low-flow).
Example/Allowed Content: Standard quartz | High-matrix | Low-flow | N/A | None | Other: specify
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — imported from LA-Q/SF-ICP-MS TAPP v4

Description: Whether the guard electrode (also called extraction lens or Fassel torch shield) was active during analysis.
Example/Allowed Content: On | Off | Not applicable (instrument does not have guard electrode)
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — imported from LA-Q/SF-ICP-MS TAPP v4

Description: Operating mass resolution of the mass analyser. Fixed at unit resolution for quadrupole instruments; selectable (low/medium/high) for sector-field instruments to balance sensitivity against interference suppression; not applicable in the same sense for multi-collector instruments running static low-resolution collection (see Faraday Cup Array Configuration and Collector Configuration for MC-specific detail).
Example/Allowed Content: e.g., Unit resolution — quadrupole (fixed) | Low resolution — SF (~300 m/Δm) | Medium resolution — SF (~3000 m/Δm) | High resolution — SF (~10000 m/Δm)
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — imported from LA-Q/SF-ICP-MS TAPP v4 (SF-ICP-MS primarily; Q-ICP-MS answer is a fixed constant)

Description: Whether a collision or reaction cell is installed and its operating mode. Applicable only to quadrupole-based instruments; single-collector sector-field and multi-collector instruments do not have collision/reaction cells (interferences are instead resolved by mass resolution or chemical separation).
Example/Allowed Content: STD (standard mode, no gas) | KED (kinetic energy discrimination, He gas) | DRC (dynamic reaction cell, reactive gas) | Not applicable (SF/MC-ICP-MS) | Other: specify
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — imported from LA-Q/SF-ICP-MS TAPP v4 (Q-ICP-MS only)

Description: Description of the multi-collector Faraday cup array: total number of Faraday cup detectors (fixed and moveable), their labelled positions, and the presence and position of any ion counter (SEM) or Daly detector. The number and span of cups constrains which isotope combinations can be simultaneously collected.
Example/Allowed Content: e.g., 'Nu Plasma HR: mixed Faraday-multiple ion counting array, [n] Faraday cups + [n] ion counters' | 'N/A (not multi-collector)'
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — imported from Solution MC-ICP-MS TAPP v3 (MC-ICP-MS only)

Description: Resistance values (Ω) of the feedback resistors in the Faraday cup amplifiers. Standard amplifiers use 10¹¹ Ω resistors; high-gain amplifiers (10¹² or 10¹³ Ω) are fitted to selected cups to improve signal-to-noise for very low-intensity beams (e.g., low-abundance Pb isotopes in young or low-U material).
Example/Allowed Content: All cups: 10¹¹ Ω | L1 (204Pb): 10¹² Ω; all others: 10¹¹ Ω | N/A (not multi-collector)
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — imported from Solution MC-ICP-MS TAPP v3 (MC-ICP-MS only)

Description: Method used to calibrate the relative gain (amplification factor) of each Faraday cup amplifier at the start of or during each analytical session. Relative gain differences between amplifiers cause systematic errors in isotope ratios if uncorrected. For instruments with ion-counting detectors, also describes the SEM-to-Faraday cross-calibration sequence.
Example/Allowed Content: Instrument internal gain calibration routine; calibrated at session start | SEM-to-Faraday cross-calibration measured per session using a known ratio solution | N/A (not multi-collector)
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — imported from Solution MC-ICP-MS TAPP v3 (MC-ICP-MS only)

Description: Instrument control and data acquisition software used to collect raw signal data, including version number.
Example/Allowed Content: e.g., 'Nu Instruments Nu Plasma TRA 2.x' | 'Thermo Qtegra 2.10' | 'Agilent MassHunter 4.6'
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — Rule 1 shared Group 3 software field (standard name mandatory in all TAPPs); Table 3 does not request acquisition software as a distinct item

Description: Software used for signal processing, background subtraction, downhole fractionation correction, and age calculation, including version number.
Example/Allowed Content: Nu Instruments Nu Plasma TRA software
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — Rule 1 shared Group 3 software field (standard name mandatory in all TAPPs); content populated 2026-07-28 by splitting the software name out of Table 3's 'Data Processing Package Used/Correction for LIEF' (Horstwood et al. 2016), leaving the LIEF correction method in the renamed Group 5 field 'Elemental Fractionation Correction'

Description: Procedure-level declaration of the analytical mode(s) this procedure covers. This TAPP is scoped to static spot ablation only, consistent with Table 3 (Horstwood et al. 2016). No mode-flag columns are used in this TAPP because only one mode is in scope.
Example/Allowed Content: Spot Analysis
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — Rule 3 — mandatory first field of Group 4 in every TAPP. Merged 2026-07-27: also covers Table 3's 'Sampling mode/pattern' item (paper example: 'Static spot ablation').

Description: Sampling mode or ablation pattern used during analysis, as described in Table 3 of Horstwood et al. (2016).
Example/Allowed Content: Spot (stationary) | Transect (continuous line scan) | Raster area (2D elemental mapping) | Stepped line profile | Other: specify
Comments: Source: Table 3 (Horstwood et al. 2016) — restructured/split for cross-TAPP consistency with LA-Q/SF-ICP-MS TAPP; reinstates Table 3's 'static' nuance as its own field, matching LA-Q/SF-ICP-MS TAPP's structure of keeping this field distinct from Analytical Mode. Content: Spot (stationary).

Description: Diameter of the laser spot as set in the acquisition method (nominal/target value).
Example/Allowed Content: 25 µm
Comments: Source: Table 3 (Horstwood et al. 2016) — restructured/split for cross-TAPP consistency with LA-Q/SF-ICP-MS TAPP; renamed and narrowed to nominal value only; measured/actual value split out to 'Spot Diameter (Measured)' below.

Description: Diameter of the laser spot as independently measured on the sample or a test material, distinct from the nominal/target value registered by the procedure.
Example/Allowed Content: 32 µm
Comments: Source: Table 3 (Horstwood et al. 2016) — restructured/split for cross-TAPP consistency with LA-Q/SF-ICP-MS TAPP; split out of the former 'Spot Diameter (µm), Nominal/Actual' field, following the target-vs-measured naming convention used elsewhere in the TAPP library (e.g. Oxide Production).

Description: Duration of each individual laser pulse. A fixed hardware property of the laser system that determines the thermal vs. non-thermal ablation regime.
Example/Allowed Content: 4 ns
Comments: Source: Table 3 (Horstwood et al. 2016) — restructured/split for cross-TAPP consistency with LA-Q/SF-ICP-MS TAPP; field renamed from 'Pulse Width (ns)' for cross-TAPP consistency.

Description: Laser pulse energy per unit area at the sample surface, the primary control on ablation rate and crater morphology.
Example/Allowed Content: 2.5 J cm⁻²
Comments: Source: Table 3 (Horstwood et al. 2016) — restructured/split for cross-TAPP consistency with LA-Q/SF-ICP-MS TAPP; field renamed from 'Fluence (J cm-2)' for cross-TAPP consistency.

Description: Laser pulse repetition rate.
Example/Allowed Content: 5 Hz
Comments: Source: Table 3 (Horstwood et al. 2016) — restructured/split for cross-TAPP consistency with LA-Q/SF-ICP-MS TAPP; field renamed from 'Repetition Rate (Hz)' for cross-TAPP consistency.

Description: Total on-sample ablation time per spot, as set in the acquisition method.
Comments: Source: Table 3 (Horstwood et al. 2016) — restructured/split for cross-TAPP consistency with LA-Q/SF-ICP-MS TAPP; field renamed from 'Ablation Duration (s)' for cross-TAPP consistency.

Description: Depth of the ablation pit produced under the registered laser conditions, the method used to measure it, and the resulting per-pulse ablation rate. Characterises the achievable depth/time resolution of the procedure.
Example/Allowed Content: 16 µm pit depth, measured using an optical microscope, SEM and interferometry, equivalent to 0.08 µm/pulse
Comments: Source: Table 3 (Horstwood et al. 2016)

Description: Spatial energy distribution of the laser beam at the sample surface, and whether a beam homogenizer is installed. A flat-top (top-hat) profile produces more uniform ablation craters than a Gaussian beam. Fixed hardware property.
Example/Allowed Content: Flat-top (top-hat) — beam homogenizer installed | Gaussian — no beam homogenizer | Not stated
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — imported from LA-Q/SF-ICP-MS TAPP v4

Description: Identity and plumbing configuration of the gas used to transport the ablated aerosol from the cell to the torch, including the procedure-registered flow rate(s).
Example/Allowed Content: 100% He in the cell (0.8 L min⁻¹), Ar make-up gas combined using a Y-piece 50% along the sample transport line to the torch.
Comments: Source: Table 3 (Horstwood et al. 2016) — restructured/split for cross-TAPP consistency with LA-Q/SF-ICP-MS TAPP; merged from separate 'Carrier Gas' and 'Cell Carrier Gas Flow (L min⁻¹)' fields for cross-TAPP consistency with LA-Q/SF-ICP-MS TAPP's combined field.

Description: ICP radiofrequency forward power. Session-tunable within procedure-defined bounds during plasma optimisation; consistent with the analogous, tunable treatment of RF Power across LA-Q/SF-ICP-MS and all three solution ICP-MS TAPPs.
Comments: Source: Table 3 (Horstwood et al. 2016) — tier confirmed 2026-07-28 as Editable (not Read-Only) after cross-checking all four sibling ICP-MS TAPPs, which unanimously use Editable

Description: Source and estimated flow rate of any make-up gas added downstream of the ablation cell, including any desolvating nebuliser used for tracer co-aspiration.
Example/Allowed Content: Sourced from Nu Instruments DSN-100 desolvating nebuliser. Neb pressure 24 psi (estimated at 0.7 L min⁻¹) Ar.
Comments: Source: Table 3 (Horstwood et al. 2016)

Description: Flow rate of the outer (coolant/plasma) argon gas stream that sustains the ICP plasma. Determines plasma volume and stability.
Example/Allowed Content: 14 L/min | 15 L/min | Other: specify
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — imported from LA-Q/SF-ICP-MS TAPP v4

Description: Flow rate of the intermediate (auxiliary) argon gas stream that positions the plasma relative to the load coil. Affects ion extraction efficiency and oxide production rates.
Example/Allowed Content: 0.8 L/min | 1.0 L/min | Other: specify
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — imported from LA-Q/SF-ICP-MS TAPP v4

Description: Whether the ICP plasma is operated under cool plasma or normal (hot) plasma conditions. Normal plasma is standard for U-(Th-)Pb geochronology; cool plasma would reduce sensitivity for these high-mass analytes and is not typically used.
Example/Allowed Content: Normal plasma (>1000 W RF) | Cool plasma (≤900 W RF) | Other: specify
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — imported from LA-Q/SF-ICP-MS TAPP v4

Description: Mass-to-charge positions (isotope masses) this procedure is designed to measure. Defines the scope of the procedure; the analyst may record the specific subset actually measured in a given session.
Comments: Source: Table 3 (Horstwood et al. 2016)

Description: The final reported chemical/isotopic variable(s) and their units — distinct from Masses Measured, which records raw acquisition scope. Covers isotope ratios (both common-Pb corrected and uncorrected, where applicable), elemental/isotopic concentrations, and any derived quantities (age, δ or ε notation) with their reference standard where relevant. For non-mass-spectrometry techniques, this field is generalised to any reported physical or chemical property and its units.
Example/Allowed Content: ²⁰⁶Pb/²³⁸U, ²⁰⁷Pb/²⁰⁶Pb, ²⁰⁷Pb/²³⁵U (corrected and uncorrected for common Pb); ²⁰⁸Pb/²³²Th (where Th measured); U concentration (µg g⁻¹); f206c; %concordance; age (Ma)
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — new generic field, informed by Table 4 of Horstwood et al. (2016) (the paper's own analytical data-reporting template, distinct from the Table 3 metadata template this TAPP is otherwise built from) and by the precedent field 'Isotope Ratio Reported' in Solution MC-ICP-MS TAPP v3

Metadata Item: Integration Time per Peak/Dwell Times; Quadrupole Settling Time Between Mass Jumps
Description: Count time (dwell time) per mass position for each measured isotope, and the settling time allowed between mass jumps, as reported in Table 3 of Horstwood et al. (2016). Applies to sequential (Q/SF) mass-hopping acquisition; for simultaneous multi-collector acquisition see Number of Blocks per Measurement, Number of Cycles per Block, and Integration Time per Cycle.
Example/Allowed Content: 200 ms for each isotope
Comments: Source: Table 3 (Horstwood et al. 2016); Q/SF-ICP-MS (sequential acquisition)

Metadata Item: Total Integration Time per Output Data Point (s)
Description: Total duty-cycle time for one complete mass-scan sweep (sum of all per-isotope dwell times and settling times), which sets the time resolution of the down-hole signal. Applies to sequential (Q/SF) acquisition.
Example/Allowed Content: ~1.2 s (N.B. this should represent the time resolution of the data)
Comments: Source: Table 3 (Horstwood et al. 2016); Q/SF-ICP-MS (sequential acquisition)

Description: Assignment of isotope masses to Faraday cup or ion counter detector positions for this procedure. For static multi-collection, one configuration applies throughout the measurement; for multi-dynamic procedures, lists all configurations and the cycling sequence. Includes interference-monitor masses collected alongside analyte isotopes.
Example/Allowed Content: e.g., L4=²⁰²Hg, L3=²⁰⁴Pb, L2=²⁰⁵Tl, L1=²⁰⁶Pb, Ax=²⁰⁷Pb, H1=²⁰⁸Pb, H2=²³²Th, H3=²³⁵U, H4=²³⁸U | N/A (not multi-collector)
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — imported from Solution MC-ICP-MS TAPP v3 (MC-ICP-MS only; Analyte-Specific)

Description: Number of measurement blocks acquired per spot. Each block typically begins with a baseline (on-peak zero) measurement before the analytical cycles. Multiple blocks allow inspection of signal stability and within-measurement drift.
Example/Allowed Content: 1 | 2 | 3 | N/A (not multi-collector)
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — imported from Solution MC-ICP-MS TAPP v3 (MC-ICP-MS only)

Description: Number of measurement cycles acquired per block. One cycle corresponds to a single set of simultaneous Faraday cup readings integrated for the duration in Integration Time per Cycle.
Example/Allowed Content: 20 | 40 | N/A (not multi-collector)
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — imported from Solution MC-ICP-MS TAPP v3 (MC-ICP-MS only)

Description: Duration of signal integration per measurement cycle. Total integration time per spot = (Number of Cycles per Block) × (Integration Time per Cycle) × (Number of Blocks per Measurement).
Example/Allowed Content: 4.194 s | 8 s | N/A (not multi-collector)
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — imported from Solution MC-ICP-MS TAPP v3 (MC-ICP-MS only)

Description: Instrument sensitivity expressed as useful yield — the percentage of sampled atoms of a given element that are ultimately detected as ions — for the analytical session, following the method cited.
Example/Allowed Content: 0.4% U ((#ions detected/#atoms sampled)*100; Schaltegger et al. 2015)
Comments: Source: Table 3 (Horstwood et al. 2016)

Description: Dead time of each ion-counting detector channel, used in dead-time correction of high count rates.
Example/Allowed Content: 6, 9 and 7 ns IC0, IC1 and IC2 resp.
Comments: Source: Table 3 (Horstwood et al. 2016)

Description: Description of any signal smoothing device or approach installed between the ablation cell and the ICP-MS to reduce pulse-to-pulse signal variability.
Example/Allowed Content: e.g., 'Squid 2.0 (laurin technik)' | 'None'
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — imported from LA-Q/SF-ICP-MS TAPP v4

Description: Description of the approach used to optimise ICP plasma conditions prior to analysis, including the reference material used for tuning and the acceptance criteria.
Example/Allowed Content: e.g., 'Daily auto-tune on 91500; optimised for max sensitivity on ²³⁸U with ThO⁺/Th⁺ <0.5%'
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — imported from LA-Q/SF-ICP-MS TAPP v4

Description: Method used to quantify plasma oxide production and the acceptance threshold applied before commencing analysis. ThO⁺/Th⁺ (mass 248/232) is the standard proxy for U-Th-Pb geochronology, directly relevant to Th/U ratio accuracy.
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — imported from LA-Q/SF-ICP-MS TAPP v4

Description: Actual oxide production ratio measured during this analytical session, using the method specified in Oxide Production Method and Threshold.
Example/Allowed Content: e.g., 'ThO⁺/Th⁺ = 0.3% (threshold <0.5% met)'
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — imported from LA-Q/SF-ICP-MS TAPP v4

Description: The mass ratio monitored to estimate doubly-charged ion (M²⁺) formation during instrument tuning.
Example/Allowed Content: ¹³⁸Ba²⁺/¹³⁸Ba⁺ (m/z 69/138) | ²³⁸U²⁺/²³⁸U⁺ (m/z 119/238)
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — imported from LA-Q/SF-ICP-MS TAPP v4

Description: Measured percentage of doubly-charged ion production for the monitored species at the time of instrument tuning.
Example/Allowed Content: <1% (threshold); 0.4% (measured)
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — imported from LA-Q/SF-ICP-MS TAPP v4

Description: Minimum warm-up time required after plasma ignition before analyses begin, and any maximum session duration enforced to maintain stable operating conditions.
Example/Allowed Content: e.g., '≥30 min warm-up after sample change; sessions ≤8 h after tuning'
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — imported from LA-Q/SF-ICP-MS TAPP v4

Description: Repeating order of primary calibration standard(s), quality control standard(s), and unknown analyses within a measurement session.
Example/Allowed Content: e.g., 'Standard-sample-standard bracketing every 5–10 unknowns'
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — imported from LA-Q/SF-ICP-MS TAPP v4

Description: Method and timing for measuring the ion beam baseline (background) during acquisition, distinct from the data-processing-level blank subtraction method (see Gas Blank, Group 5). For LA-ICP-MS, baseline is measured with the laser off (gas blank), typically before each ablation or block.
Example/Allowed Content: e.g., 'Laser-off background measured for [n] cycles before each block' | 'N/A (not multi-collector)'
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — imported from Solution MC-ICP-MS TAPP v3 (MC-ICP-MS only; content adapted for laser-off baseline timing instead of solution-introduction beam-deflector/acid-blank methods)

Description: Location of the analysis on the sample surface: stage coordinates (X, Y) or a description relative to a named reference feature (e.g., mineral rim, growth zone identified by imaging).
Example/Allowed Content: e.g., 'X = 12350 µm, Y = 8760 µm (stage coordinates)' | 'Core domain, per CL imaging'
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — imported from LA-Q/SF-ICP-MS TAPP v4

Description: Number of replicate spot analyses performed on the same grain or nominal location in this session.
Example/Allowed Content: e.g., 1 (single spot) | 3 (three replicate spots per grain)
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — imported from LA-Q/SF-ICP-MS TAPP v4

Description: Whether the procedure uses a single acquisition pass or multiple sequential runs on the same sample location, each optimised for different analytical objectives.
Example/Allowed Content: Single run | N/A | Other: specify
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — imported from LA-Q/SF-ICP-MS TAPP v4

Description: Mode used to collect ion signal across the monitored masses. In peak hopping mode, the quadrupole jumps sequentially between pre-set mass positions and dwells at each peak. Applicable only to quadrupole-based instruments.
Example/Allowed Content: Peak hopping | Scanning | Not applicable (SF/MC-ICP-MS) | Other: specify
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — imported from LA-Q/SF-ICP-MS TAPP v4 (Q-ICP-MS only)

Description: Type of collision gas used in KED mode for polyatomic interference suppression. Applicable only to quadrupole-based instruments with a collision/reaction cell.
Example/Allowed Content: He | H2 | Not applicable (SF/MC-ICP-MS or STD mode) | Other: specify
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — imported from LA-Q/SF-ICP-MS TAPP v4 (Q-ICP-MS only)

Description: Flow rate of the collision gas in KED mode. Higher flow rates provide greater interference suppression at the cost of analyte sensitivity.
Example/Allowed Content: 3.5 mL/min | Not applicable (SF/MC-ICP-MS or STD mode)
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — imported from LA-Q/SF-ICP-MS TAPP v4 (Q-ICP-MS only)

Description: Kinetic energy discrimination offset voltage applied at the exit of the collision cell in KED mode.
Example/Allowed Content: −5 V | Not applicable (SF/MC-ICP-MS or STD mode)
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — imported from LA-Q/SF-ICP-MS TAPP v4 (Q-ICP-MS only)

Description: Type of reactive gas introduced into the dynamic reaction cell (DRC) for interference removal through ion-molecule reactions.
Example/Allowed Content: NH3 | O2 | Not applicable (SF/MC-ICP-MS or DRC mode not used) | Other: specify
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — imported from LA-Q/SF-ICP-MS TAPP v4 (Q-ICP-MS only)

Description: Flow rate of the reactive gas introduced into the dynamic reaction cell (DRC).
Example/Allowed Content: 0.4 mL/min | Not applicable (SF/MC-ICP-MS or DRC mode not used)
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — imported from LA-Q/SF-ICP-MS TAPP v4 (Q-ICP-MS only)

Description: Mass resolution mode assigned to each analyte in this procedure. The selected resolution determines which polyatomic interferences (e.g., ¹⁸⁶W¹⁶O⁺ on ²⁰²Hg, relevant to common-Pb correction) are physically resolved by the magnetic sector. Applicable only to sector-field instruments.
Example/Allowed Content: All LR (m/Δm ≈ 300) | LR: Pb, U, Th; MR: Hg-interference-affected masses | N/A (not sector-field)
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — imported from LA-Q/SF-ICP-MS TAPP v4 (SF-ICP-MS only; Analyte-Specific)

Description: Electric scan range used for peak acquisition, expressed as percentage of the centre mass. Varies the accelerating voltage to cover nearby masses without re-scanning the magnet. Applicable only to sector-field instruments.
Example/Allowed Content: 15% | 10% | N/A (not sector-field)
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — imported from LA-Q/SF-ICP-MS TAPP v4 (SF-ICP-MS only)

Description: Whether each mass peak is scanned three times per cycle and the results averaged, to reduce noise from short-term magnetic field instabilities. Applicable only to sector-field instruments with this capability.
Example/Allowed Content: Y | N | N/A (not sector-field)
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — imported from LA-Q/SF-ICP-MS TAPP v4 (SF-ICP-MS only)

Description: Supplementary methodological context not captured by the structured fields above, as reported in Table 3 of Horstwood et al. (2016) — in the source paper's own example, notes on ablation-cell and sample-line configuration for depth-profiling/single-pulse ablation studies, a variant not otherwise in scope for this single-mode (Spot Analysis) TAPP.
Example/Allowed Content: Depth profiling and single-pulse ablation studies used a low-volume ablation cell, sample line of 3 m from ablation cell to torch and a 20 s wait time between ablations. Cell washout time was ca. 0.8 s to 1% of peak signal.
Comments: Source: Table 3 (Horstwood et al. 2016)

Description: Duration of the background (gas blank) measurement and how it is applied to correct the ablation signal.
Example/Allowed Content: 30 s on-peak zero subtracted
Comments: Source: Table 3 (Horstwood et al. 2016)

Description: Method used to correct for laser-induced elemental fractionation (LIEF), including any assumption about reference-material/sample behaviour equivalence, as reported in Table 3 of Horstwood et al. (2016).
Example/Allowed Content: LIEF correction assumes reference material and samples behave identically.
Comments: Source: Table 3 (Horstwood et al. 2016) — restructured/split for cross-TAPP consistency with LA-Q/SF-ICP-MS TAPP; field renamed from 'Data Processing Package Used/Correction for LIEF' for cross-TAPP consistency; software-name content moved to Group 3's 'Data Reduction Software'.

Description: Primary strategy used to correct for instrumental isotopic mass fractionation (mass bias/mass discrimination).
Example/Allowed Content: Internal normalization
Comments: Source: Table 3 (Horstwood et al. 2016) — restructured/split for cross-TAPP consistency with LA-Q/SF-ICP-MS TAPP; split out of the former 'Mass Discrimination' field, matching the field structure of Solution MC-ICP-MS TAPP v3. Table 3's Tl-U tracer approach corresponds to internal normalization.

Metadata Item: Internal Normalization Element and Isotope Ratio
Description: Element and isotope ratio used as the internal normalization standard for mass bias correction, and how the resulting correction is applied to analyte ratios.
Example/Allowed Content: Tl-U tracer solution used for mass bias correction, with 207Pb/206Pb and 206Pb/238U additionally normalised to reference material
Comments: Source: Table 3 (Horstwood et al. 2016) — restructured/split for cross-TAPP consistency with LA-Q/SF-ICP-MS TAPP; split out of the former 'Mass Discrimination' field, matching Solution MC-ICP-MS TAPP v3's 'Internal Normalization Element and Isotope Ratio' field.

Description: Mathematical law used to parameterize instrumental isotope mass fractionation as a function of mass difference. Not stated in Table 3 (Horstwood et al. 2016) for the worked example; the exponential law is most widely used and theoretically best justified for MC-ICP-MS.
Example/Allowed Content: Exponential | Linear | Power | Not stated
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — imported from Solution MC-ICP-MS TAPP v3 (primarily relevant to MC-ICP-MS mass bias correction)

Description: Whether a common-Pb correction was applied, and if so, the model composition (e.g., Stacey and Kramers 1975) and its uncertainty used in the correction.
Example/Allowed Content: No common-Pb correction applied to the data.
Comments: Source: Table 3 (Horstwood et al. 2016)

Description: Uncertainty level at which ages/ratios are quoted (e.g., 1σ, 2σ) and the method used to propagate component uncertainties (e.g., quadratic addition) into the final reported value.
Example/Allowed Content: Ages are quoted at 2s absolute, propagation is by quadratic addition. Reproducibility and age uncertainty of reference material and common-Pb composition uncertainty are propagated where appropriate.
Comments: Source: Table 3 (Horstwood et al. 2016)

Description: Documents cases where different analytes are calibrated using different strategies within the same session. If a single strategy applies uniformly, record that here.
Example/Allowed Content: Single strategy: matrix-matched primary reference material for all analytes | N/A | Other: specify
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — imported from LA-Q/SF-ICP-MS TAPP v4

Description: Whether an empirical correction was applied to account for systematic differences in laser-induced elemental fractionation (LIEF) patterns between the external calibration standard and the sample matrix.
Example/Allowed Content: e.g., 'Not applicable (matrix-matched mineral standard used)' | 'Applied: specify'
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — imported from LA-Q/SF-ICP-MS TAPP v4

Description: Approach used to select the stable signal interval for integration during data reduction, and to exclude anomalous signals from inclusions, cracks, or mixed domains. Central to interpreting excess scatter/MSWD in the resulting age population.
Example/Allowed Content: Manual visual inspection per analysis | Automated threshold (specify software and threshold) | Fixed time window applied uniformly
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — imported from LA-Q/SF-ICP-MS TAPP v4

Description: Actual integration time used for the ablation signal in this analysis. Determined at analysis time by applying the Signal Integration Interval Method to the time-resolved signal.
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — imported from LA-Q/SF-ICP-MS TAPP v4

Description: Method used to identify and remove anomalous signal spikes arising from micronuggets, inclusions, cracks, or instrument artifacts during time-resolved signal processing.
Example/Allowed Content: e.g., 'Significant single spikes visually identified and removed' | 'No filtering applied'
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — imported from LA-Q/SF-ICP-MS TAPP v4

Description: Whether isobaric interference corrections were applied for any measured isotope in this procedure. A procedure-level Boolean; element-specific detail is in Interfering Species and Interference Correction Method.
Example/Allowed Content: Yes | No
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — imported from LA-Q/SF-ICP-MS TAPP v4

Description: Elemental or molecular species overlapping with the measured isotope, relevant to U-Th-Pb geochronology (e.g., ²⁰⁴Hg on ²⁰⁴Pb, relevant to the Common-Pb Correction field above).
Example/Allowed Content: e.g., '²⁰⁴Hg on ²⁰⁴Pb' | 'None'
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — imported from LA-Q/SF-ICP-MS TAPP v4

Description: Equation or procedure used to correct for isobaric interferences, including the reference material or monitor isotope used to characterise it.
Example/Allowed Content: e.g., '²⁰²Hg monitored to correct ²⁰⁴Hg on ²⁰⁴Pb via natural ²⁰⁴Hg/²⁰²Hg' | 'None'
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — imported from LA-Q/SF-ICP-MS TAPP v4

Description: Mass balance approach used to calculate sample mass fractions from spike-sample isotope ratio measurements, relevant when a concentration spike (e.g., ²³⁵U, as in Table 3's own worked example) is co-aspirated. Record 'None' if isotope dilution is not used.
Example/Allowed Content: e.g., 'IUPAC isotope dilution equations' | 'None'
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — imported from LA-Q/SF-ICP-MS TAPP v4

Description: The pair of enriched isotopes used to construct a double spike for combined mass bias and/or common-Pb correction. Both isotopes must be naturally rare and free from isobaric interferences. Record 'N/A' if double-spike method is not used.
Example/Allowed Content: e.g., ²⁰⁴Pb–²⁰⁷Pb | N/A
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — imported from Solution MC-ICP-MS TAPP v3 (MC-ICP-MS only, double-spike procedures)

Description: Target proportion of double-spike signal relative to total analyte signal in the spiked mixture. An optimal mixing ratio minimises error propagation through the double-spike inversion. Record 'N/A' if double-spike method is not used.
Example/Allowed Content: e.g., ~0.4 (spike fraction) | N/A
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — imported from Solution MC-ICP-MS TAPP v3 (MC-ICP-MS only, double-spike procedures)

Description: Mathematical algorithm used to simultaneously solve for the true sample isotope ratio and the mass fractionation factor from the measured spike-sample mixture. Record 'N/A' if double-spike method is not used.
Example/Allowed Content: e.g., Rudge et al. (2009) Double Spike Toolbox | N/A
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — imported from Solution MC-ICP-MS TAPP v3 (MC-ICP-MS only, double-spike procedures)

Description: Procedure applied to identify and minimise memory effects from high-concentration elements in the previous sample or standard that may contaminate subsequent analyses.
Example/Allowed Content: e.g., 'Extended washout between high-U standards and unknowns' | 'None required'
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — imported from LA-Q/SF-ICP-MS TAPP v4

Description: Any post-acquisition normalization applied to correct for systematic biases identified from secondary reference materials.
Example/Allowed Content: e.g., 'None' | 'Applied: specify'
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — imported from LA-Q/SF-ICP-MS TAPP v4

Description: Primary reference material used to calibrate the instrument and convert raw signal intensities to ages/isotope ratios. Include citation for the accepted values used.
Example/Allowed Content: 91500 (Wiedenbeck et al. 1995)
Comments: Source: Table 3 (Horstwood et al. 2016) — restructured/split for cross-TAPP consistency with LA-Q/SF-ICP-MS TAPP; split out of the former 'Calibration Strategy' + 'Reference Material Information' fields, re-partitioned along LA-Q/SF-ICP-MS TAPP's primary/secondary axis.

Description: Quality-control reference material(s) analysed as unknowns alongside samples in the same session to assess accuracy and monitor drift. Include citation/accepted values for each.
Example/Allowed Content: Plesovice (Slama et al. 2008); GJ1, 206Pb/238U 0.097877 ± 0.07%, 207Pb/206Pb 0.060171 ± 0.08% (in-house CA-TIMS, this study)
Comments: Source: Table 3 (Horstwood et al. 2016) — restructured/split for cross-TAPP consistency with LA-Q/SF-ICP-MS TAPP; split out of the former 'Calibration Strategy' + 'Reference Material Information' fields, re-partitioned along LA-Q/SF-ICP-MS TAPP's primary/secondary axis.

Metadata Item: Within-Session Analytical Precision and Assessment Method
Description: Reproducibility of repeated measurements within a single analytical session. Assessment method specifies the reference material used, number of replicates n, and the statistic reported.
Example/Allowed Content: Plesovice — Wtd ave 206Pb/238U age = 338 ± 3 (2s, MSWD = 0.9, n = 8); GJ-1 — Wtd ave 206Pb/238U age = 602 ± 5 (2s, MSWD = 1.1, n = 7)
Comments: Source: Table 3 (Horstwood et al. 2016) — restructured/split for cross-TAPP consistency with LA-Q/SF-ICP-MS TAPP; split out of the former 'Quality Control/Validation' field, which reported within-session validation-material weighted-average ages, MSWD and n; this destination inherits that content directly.

Metadata Item: Between-Session (Long-Term) Analytical Precision and Assessment Method
Description: Reproducibility of measurements across multiple analytical sessions over weeks to months. Not addressed in Table 3 of Horstwood et al. (2016), which reports only within-session validation results.
Example/Allowed Content: e.g., '2σ RSD = X% for 206Pb/238U age on [RM] across N sessions over M months'
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — new field with no Table 3 precedent, added alongside the split of 'Quality Control/Validation' to complete the precision/accuracy structure used in LA-Q/SF-ICP-MS TAPP and Solution MC-ICP-MS TAPP; Advanced (not Basic) because no paper content exists to inherit, unlike its two sibling fields from the same split

Description: Offset between measured and accepted reference values for secondary reference materials. Table 3's validation weighted-average ages, compared against each material's independently accepted age (cited in Secondary Reference Materials above), serve as the accuracy statement for this worked example.
Example/Allowed Content: Plesovice measured weighted-average age (338 ± 3 Ma) compared against accepted age (337.13 ± 0.37 Ma, Slama et al. 2008); GJ-1 measured weighted-average age (602 ± 5 Ma) compared against accepted age from Reference Material Information
Comments: Source: Table 3 (Horstwood et al. 2016) — restructured/split for cross-TAPP consistency with LA-Q/SF-ICP-MS TAPP; split out of the former 'Quality Control/Validation' field; reframed as a bias-vs-accepted-value statement using the accepted ages already cited in Secondary Reference Materials, since Table 3's compact example reports precision and accuracy together in one value.

Description: How often the primary calibration standard is measured relative to unknown samples within a session, i.e. the bracketing interval used to monitor and correct for instrumental drift. Implied but not stated explicitly in Table 3 (Horstwood et al. 2016) via the validation-material n counts.
Example/Allowed Content: e.g., 'Before and after every 10 unknowns' | 'Start and end of session only'
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — imported from LA-Q/SF-ICP-MS TAPP v4

Description: Session detection limit for U, Th, and/or Pb, demonstrating the reliability of reported concentrations near the detection limit. Not requested by Table 3 of Horstwood et al. (2016), which focuses on age uncertainty rather than elemental detection limits.
Example/Allowed Content: e.g., '0.05 ppm U (3σ background)' | 'Range: 0.02–0.4 ppm across U, Th, Pb'
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — Rule 1 shared Group 6 QC term (gap vs. Table 3)

Description: Reference or description of the method used to calculate the session detection limit reported above.
Example/Allowed Content: e.g., '3σ of background ion counts per Longerich et al. (1996)'
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — Rule 1 shared Group 6 QC term (gap vs. Table 3)

Description: Reference or description of the method used to calculate the limit of quantification: the lowest concentration reliably measurable with acceptable precision and accuracy.
Example/Allowed Content: 10σ blank | 10× DL | S/N ≥ 10 | Other: specify
Comments: Source: In-house TAPP rule — imported from LA-Q/SF-ICP-MS TAPP v4
